object_types.name: Person
object_types.definition: Anyone in the system, identified by a person ID.

source_references.excerpt: We track persons generally -- anyone in the system is a person with a person ID.
anyone in the system is a person with a person ID

object_types.name: Employee
object_types.definition: A person who is employed; every employee is also a person, identified the same way.

source_references.excerpt: Employees are persons; every employee is also a person, identified the same way.

object_types.name: Manager
object_types.definition: An employee with extra responsibilities; every manager is an employee.

source_references.excerpt: A manager is an employee with extra responsibilities. Every manager is an employee, and through that, a person.

object_types.name: Department
object_types.definition: An organizational unit identified by a department code, having employees and optionally a manager.

source_references.excerpt: Each department has a department code.

object_types.name: DepartmentCode
object_types.definition: The identifying code for a Department.

source_references.excerpt: Each department has a department code.

object_types.name: DepartmentName
object_types.definition: The name of a department, e.g. 'Payroll' or 'Field Operations'; unique across departments.

source_references.excerpt: Departments also each have a department name, like "Payroll" or "Field Operations", and no two share a name.

ambiguities.description: Managers are not required to manage a department ('some managers are between assignments and manage none'). Is there any uniqueness constraint on the Department side of Manager manages Department -- can a department have more than one manager, or is it also at most one manager per department? The transcript only states the manager side's cardinality explicitly.

ambiguities.description: The reference mode for Person, Employee, and Manager is stated to be the same ('identified the same way'), implying they share person_id as identification, but it's not explicit whether Employee or Manager could have an additional independent identifier (e.g., employee number). Confirm no separate employee/manager identifier is needed.
